ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\angle AOE = \angle BOE = 15^\circ$, $EF \parallel OB$, $EC \perp OB$. If $EC = 2$, what is the length of $EF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct $EG \perp OA$ at $G$, as shown in the figure:\\
Since $EF \parallel OB$, $\angle AOE = \angle BOE = 15^\circ$, and $EC \perp OB$,\\
it follows that $\angle OEF = \angle COE = 15^\circ$ and $EG = CE = 2$,\\
Since $\angle AOE = 15^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle EFG = 15^\circ + 15^\circ = 30^\circ$,\\
Therefore, $EF = 2EG = \boxed{4}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, O is on the left, and OA is a horizontal ray to the right; OB is an upper oblique ray; OE is located between OA and OB. Point F is on OA, point E is on OE, and point C is on OB. Segment EF connects from F to E, with direction parallel to OB; segment EC connects from E to C, and is perpendicular to OB. Reasoning according to the specified coordinate method: take O as the origin and OA as the x-axis. From the figure and the given conditions, it can be known that the angle between OE and OA is 15°, and the angle between OB and OE is also 15°, so the angle between OB and OA is 30°. Let OE = r, then the coordinates of E are (r cos15°, r sin15°). Because EC is the perpendicular distance from point E to line OB, and the angle between OE and OB is 15°, EC = r sin15°. It is known that EC = 2, therefore r sin15° = 2. At the same time, the vertical height from E to the x-axis OA is exactly r sin15°, so the height of E is 2. Since EF ∥ OB, the angle between EF and OA is 30°. The vertical component from F to E is EF·sin30°, which is exactly equal to the height of E, 2. Therefore EF·sin30° = 2. Also sin30° = 1/2, so EF = 2 ÷ (1/2) = 4. Final answer: 4
